seoTitle: How to Connect Claude to Notion for Smarter Notes
metaDescription: Connect Claude to your Notion workspace through Settings > Customize > Connectors, see what it can read and update, and understand the permission limits first.
intro: Connecting Claude to Notion lets it search, read, and update the pages you already keep notes and project docs in, instead of you copying context back and forth between two tabs. The setup lives inside Claude's own Settings, under Customize, not inside Notion, which is the part that trips people up on a first attempt. This guide walks through opening Connectors, authorizing Notion, and what Claude can see and do once it's connected, plus where the integration is most useful for project and knowledge-base pages. It also covers the permission boundary worth understanding upfront if you're connecting a workspace you don't fully own.
prerequisites: A Notion account with access to the workspace (or at least the specific pages) you want Claude to read

steps.heading: Open Settings from Claude's account menu
steps.body: From Claude's home screen, click your account icon in the bottom-left corner to open the account menu, then choose Settings. If you're already mid-conversation, there's a shortcut: click the plus icon in the message box, hover Connectors, and choose Manage connectors, which lands in the same place. Connectors are tied to your account, not the device, so this setup covers Claude everywhere you sign in afterward.

image.caption: Claude's account menu, opened from the icon in the bottom-left corner. Settings is the first item, and it's where the Notion connection starts.

steps.heading: Open Connectors and search for Notion
steps.body: Inside Settings, open Customize and select Connectors. Click the plus icon next to Connectors to browse what's available, the same list published on its own at claude.ai/directory. Search for Notion; its card describes it as a way to search, update, and power workflows across tools. Click Connect to start the authorization flow.

image.caption: The Connectors section inside Claude's Settings, with Notion listed and a plus icon to start the connection.

steps.heading: Authorize access to your workspace
steps.body: Clicking Connect redirects you through Notion's own sign-in flow, where you choose which workspace to connect and confirm the permissions Claude is requesting. Claude inherits whatever access your Notion account already has. If you're a guest in someone else's workspace, not its owner, you can only grant Claude the pages you personally have permission to see, not the whole workspace. If you belong to more than one Notion workspace, Notion asks you to pick one explicitly, so check you're selecting the right one before confirming.

steps.heading: See what Claude can now reach
steps.body: Once connected, Claude can search pages in the authorized workspace and read their contents when you ask, pulling structured detail like a nested bullet list documenting a system's functions instead of you scanning the page yourself. Ask about a page directly and get an answer grounded in what's written there.

image.caption: A Notion page with nested, structured content. This is the kind of detail Claude can search and reference directly once the workspace is connected.

steps.heading: Use it for project docs and knowledge bases
steps.body: The integration is most useful on pages with real structure already in place: project trackers, system documentation, onboarding wikis. Claude can navigate that structure instead of treating the page as one undifferentiated block of text. Ask it to summarize a page, compare details across a few related pages, or draft new content that follows the format of what's already there. For teams, it's a faster way to onboard someone into a documentation-heavy workspace, since they can ask questions instead of reading every page cover to cover.

steps.heading: Manage or disconnect it later
steps.body: Revisit Settings > Customize > Connectors to confirm Notion is still listed, and disconnect from the same screen if you switch workspaces or want to reset access. Because Claude only sees what your Notion account can see, losing access to a page in Notion, being removed as a collaborator, for example, automatically narrows what Claude can retrieve too. There's no separate permission system layered on top of Notion's own.

steps.heading: Write prompts that point Claude at the right page
steps.body: Once a workspace has several connected pages, name the page or its parent section in your question instead of describing the topic loosely; that gets a more accurate answer faster. Treat Claude's Notion search the way you'd treat Notion's own search bar: specific titles and section names narrow results quickly, while a vague topic description can pull in more pages than you wanted referenced.

troubleshooting.problem: Claude says it can't find a page you know exists
troubleshooting.cause: Claude only sees what your own Notion account has permission to see. If you're a guest on that workspace, or the page's sharing settings changed, the page is invisible to Claude too, not a sign the connector failed.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your own access to the page inside Notion first. If you can't open it there, reconnecting in Claude won't help.

troubleshooting.problem: Notion shows as connected but Claude can't act on it
troubleshooting.cause: The underlying authorization can expire or get revoked from Notion's side without Claude showing an obvious error.
troubleshooting.fix: Go to Settings > Customize > Connectors, disconnect Notion, then reconnect to refresh the authorization.

faq.question: Where do I connect Claude to Notion?
faq.answer: Open Claude's account menu, go to Settings, then Customize, and select Connectors. Click the plus icon, search for Notion, and click Connect to start the authorization flow.

faq.question: What does connecting Claude to Notion let it do?
faq.answer: Claude can search pages in your authorized Notion workspace and reference their real content when answering, instead of you copying notes into the chat yourself.

faq.question: Can Claude see my entire Notion workspace?
faq.answer: Only the pages your own Notion account already has permission to see. If you're a guest in someone else's workspace, Claude is limited to the same pages you can open there.

faq.question: Is this integration only useful for individuals?
faq.answer: No. It works for teams too, particularly for onboarding someone into a documentation-heavy workspace by letting them ask Claude questions instead of reading every page manually.

faq.question: How do I disconnect Notion later?
faq.answer: Go back to Settings > Customize > Connectors, find Notion, and remove it from there. That's the same screen used to connect it in the first place.

verifiedNote: Screens and the account-menu entry point come from the original recording. The connector setup path has since changed: Anthropic moved it from a standalone Directory tab to Settings > Customize > Connectors, confirmed against Claude's official help center and tutorial pages in September 2026, and this guide's navigation steps were corrected to match. The permission-inheritance behavior (a guest sees only what they can already see in Notion) was confirmed there too.
